**Ace in Blackjack – the “soft” card**

| Situation | How the Ace is treated |
|-----------|------------------------|
| **Single Ace in a hand** | It can count as **11** *or* **1**, whichever gives the best total without busting. If counting it as 11 would bust the hand, it automatically becomes 1. |
| **Two Aces together** | One Ace is counted as 11 and the other as 1, giving a “soft 12.” If you later draw a card that would bust the hand, the Ace that was 11 can drop to 1. |
| **Natural Blackjack** | An Ace plus any 10‑value card (10, J, Q, K) is a “blackjack” worth 21. This is the highest possible hand and usually pays 3:2. |
| **Splitting Aces** | Most casinos allow you to split a pair of Aces. After splitting, each Ace is treated as 11 until you draw a card that would bust the hand, at which point it can drop to 1. Many tables also restrict you to only one additional card on each split Ace (no further hits). |
| **Doubling Down on Split Aces** | Some rules let you double down on each split Ace if you’re allowed to double after a split. |

**Bottom line:** An Ace is a flexible card that can be worth 1 or 11, whichever keeps your hand from busting while maximizing its value.
